prompt: Name an informal tool or power presidents use to shape policy.
hint: Think about communication, persuasion, or presidential directives.

answers.label: Executive agreement
aliases: international agreement without a senate treaty vote
answers.explanation: An international agreement without the Senate’s two-thirds treaty vote must still rest on valid legal authority.

answers.label: Executive order

answers.label: Signing statement
aliases: explains how the president interprets a law
answers.explanation: A statement issued when signing legislation explains the administration’s interpretation; it does not change the law.

answers.label: Bargaining and persuasion
answers.explanation: Presidents negotiate for support. Lawmakers still choose how to vote.

answers.label: Bully pulpit
aliases: using public attention to build support
using the presidency to gain public support
using public speeches to build support
answers.explanation: The president uses public attention to highlight issues and build support. Public support does not guarantee legislation.

answers.label: Going public
answers.explanation: Presidents appeal directly to the public to build support for their priorities.

answers.label: Agenda setting
answers.explanation: Presidents draw attention to policy priorities and shape what government discusses.

prompt: Name a power of Congress.
hint: Name one thing that fits.

answers.label: Tax
answers.explanation: Article I gives Congress the power to lay and collect taxes.

answers.label: Borrow money
answers.explanation: Congress may borrow money on the credit of the United States.

answers.label: Coin money
answers.explanation: Congress has the constitutional power to coin money and regulate its value.

answers.label: Regulate interstate commerce
answers.explanation: Congress may regulate commerce among the states, with foreign nations, and with Indian tribes.

answers.label: Declare war
answers.explanation: Congress has the power to declare war; the president commands the armed forces.

answers.label: Raise and support armies
answers.explanation: Congress raises and supports armies and controls military funding.

answers.label: Establish post offices
answers.explanation: Congress can establish post offices and post roads.

answers.label: Provide and maintain a navy
answers.explanation: Article I gives Congress the power to provide and maintain a navy.

answers.label: Set naturalization rules
answers.explanation: Congress sets uniform rules for becoming a U.S. citizen.

answers.label: Set bankruptcy laws
answers.explanation: Congress can establish uniform bankruptcy laws.

answers.label: Protect inventions and writings
answers.explanation: Congress can secure limited exclusive rights for inventors and authors.

answers.label: Establish lower federal courts
answers.explanation: Congress can establish federal courts below the Supreme Court.

answers.label: Set weights and measures
answers.explanation: Congress can set national standards for weights and measures.

answers.label: Punish counterfeiting
answers.explanation: Congress can punish counterfeiting of U.S. securities and coin.

answers.label: Make necessary and proper laws
answers.explanation: Congress can make laws needed to carry out its enumerated powers.

answers.label: Regulate foreign commerce
answers.explanation: Congress regulates commerce with foreign nations.

answers.label: Regulate commerce with Indian tribes
answers.explanation: Article I includes commerce with Indian tribes.

answers.label: Punish piracy and offenses on the high seas
answers.explanation: Congress defines and punishes piracy and felonies on the high seas.

answers.label: Punish offenses against the law of nations
answers.explanation: Article I expressly grants this power.

answers.label: Grant letters of marque and reprisal
answers.explanation: Congress can authorize letters of marque and reprisal.

answers.label: Make rules concerning captures
answers.explanation: Congress sets rules concerning wartime captures.

answers.label: Make rules for the armed forces
answers.explanation: Congress makes rules governing the land and naval forces.

answers.label: Organize and call forth the militia
answers.explanation: Congress can organize, arm, discipline, and call forth the militia within constitutional limits.

answers.label: Govern the federal district
answers.explanation: Congress has legislative authority over the seat of government.

answers.label: Spend for the general welfare
answers.explanation: The taxing and spending clause covers debts, common defense, and general welfare.

answers.label: Override a veto
answers.explanation: Two-thirds of each chamber can override a regular presidential veto.

answers.label: Power of the Purse
answers.explanation: Congress's authority to provide, limit, or withhold funding, which it can use to influence executive agencies and programs.

answers.label: Oversight
answers.explanation: Efforts by Congress to ensure executive branch agencies and officials are acting legally and in accordance with congressional goals.

answers.label: Impeachment
answers.explanation: The House can impeach the president; conviction and removal require a two-thirds vote of senators present in a Senate trial.

answers.label: Senate Confirmation
answers.explanation: The Senate's approval of many presidential nominees, including Cabinet officers, ambassadors, and federal judges.

answers.label: Consent to treaties
answers.explanation: Treaties require consent from two-thirds of senators present before the president ratifies them.

answers.label: Pass laws
answers.explanation: Congress passes legislation; a bill must clear both chambers and the constitutional presentment process.

answers.explanation: Heads a state executive branch.

answers.explanation: Heads many city governments.

answers.label: County executive
answers.explanation: Heads administration in many county governments.

answers.explanation: Directs administration in council manager governments.

answers.label: Village president

prompt: Name a legislative position at the federal, state, or local level.
hint: Name one office or concept that fits.

answers.label: U.S. senator
answers.explanation: Serves in the U.S. Senate.

answers.label: U.S. representative
answers.explanation: Serves in the U.S. House of Representatives.

answers.label: State senator
answers.explanation: Serves in a state senate.

answers.label: State representative
answers.explanation: Serves in a state legislature.

answers.label: City council member
answers.explanation: Serves on a local legislative council.

answers.label: County commissioner
aliases: member of the board of supervisors
answers.explanation: Serves on a county legislative body.

answers.label: Speaker of the House
answers.explanation: Leads a legislative chamber.

answers.label: Town meeting member
answers.explanation: Participates in a town meeting legislature.

answers.label: House Majority Leader
answers.explanation: A leader of the House majority party who helps set its legislative priorities and build support for bills.

answers.label: Senate Majority Leader

answers.label: Whip
answers.explanation: A party leader who counts votes and encourages members to support the party’s position.

answers.label: President Pro Tempore
answers.explanation: The senator who acts in the absence of the vice president; usually the most senior senator of the majority party.

answers.label: House Minority Leader
answers.explanation: Leads the minority party in the House.

answers.label: Senate Minority Leader
answers.explanation: Leads the minority party in the Senate.

answers.label: President of the Senate

answers.explanation: The vice president presides over the Senate and can break tied votes.

prompt: Name a key term or concept connected to Baker v. Carr.
hint: Name one office or concept that fits.

answers.label: Equal Protection Clause
answers.explanation: Baker made an Equal Protection challenge to legislative apportionment justiciable.

answers.label: Fourteenth Amendment
answers.explanation: Contains the Equal Protection Clause used in the case.

answers.label: Justiciability
answers.explanation: The Court could hear this kind of apportionment challenge.

answers.label: Political question doctrine
answers.explanation: Baker distinguished a justiciable Equal Protection claim from a nonjusticiable political question.

answers.label: Malapportionment
answers.explanation: Unequal legislative district populations were central to the dispute.

answers.label: Apportionment
answers.explanation: The case concerned the apportionment of legislative seats.

answers.label: Redistricting
answers.explanation: Baker helped open the door to federal court review of districting disputes.

answers.label: One person one vote
answers.explanation: A related district population principle developed in later cases such as Reynolds v. Sims; Baker itself opened the courthouse door.

answers.label: Federal court jurisdiction
answers.explanation: The case addressed whether federal courts could decide the claim.

answers.label: Judicial review
answers.explanation: Courts can review constitutional claims about representation.

answers.label: Gerrymandering
answers.explanation: A related districting issue. Baker concerned unequal apportionment and justiciability, rather than deciding a partisan gerrymandering claim.

prompt: Name a key term or concept connected to McCulloch v. Maryland.
hint: Name one office or concept that fits.

answers.label: Necessary and Proper Clause
answers.explanation: Supports congressional choice of appropriate means to carry out enumerated powers.

answers.label: Implied powers
answers.explanation: Congress could create a national bank as a means to carry out its constitutional responsibilities.

answers.label: Supremacy Clause
answers.explanation: Valid federal law prevails over conflicting state action.

answers.label: Federalism
answers.explanation: The dispute concerned the relationship between national and state authority.

answers.label: National bank
aliases: second bank of the United States
answers.explanation: The case involved Congress’s authority to create a national bank.

answers.label: Intergovernmental tax immunity
aliases: states cannot tax the federal government
state cannot tax a federal bank
power to tax is power to destroy
the power to tax involves the power to destroy
power to tax involves power to destroy
no state tax on federal bank
answers.explanation: Maryland could not tax the federal bank in a way that interfered with federal constitutional powers.

answers.label: Enumerated powers
answers.explanation: Implied means help Congress carry out its enumerated powers.

answers.label: Limited government
answers.explanation: The Constitution limits state interference with valid federal action.

answers.label: Broad constitutional interpretation
answers.explanation: The decision interpreted national powers broadly rather than requiring every means to be expressly listed.

answers.label: State sovereignty
answers.explanation: The decision limited Maryland’s sovereign taxing authority where it interfered with valid federal powers.

answers.label: Judicial review
answers.explanation: Chief Justice John Marshall’s Court interpreted national powers and constitutional supremacy in deciding the dispute.

answers.label: John Marshall
answers.explanation: Chief Justice John Marshall wrote the Court’s opinion in McCulloch v. Maryland.

prompt: Name a clause in the U.S. Constitution.
hint: Name one office or concept that fits.

answers.label: Supremacy Clause
answers.explanation: Makes the Constitution and valid federal laws the supreme law of the land.

answers.label: Necessary and Proper Clause
answers.explanation: Allows Congress to choose appropriate means for its enumerated powers.

answers.label: Commerce Clause
answers.explanation: Authorizes Congress to regulate commerce with foreign nations, among states, and with Indian tribes.

answers.label: Full Faith and Credit Clause
answers.explanation: Addresses state recognition of other states’ public acts, records, and judicial proceedings.

answers.label: Privileges and Immunities Clause
answers.explanation: Protects citizens of each state in the privileges and immunities of citizens in the several states.

answers.label: Equal Protection Clause
answers.explanation: The Fourteenth Amendment prohibits states from denying equal protection of the laws.

answers.label: Due Process Clause
answers.explanation: The Fifth and Fourteenth Amendments contain due process protections.

answers.label: Establishment Clause
answers.explanation: Prohibits laws respecting an establishment of religion.

answers.label: Free Exercise Clause
answers.explanation: Protects free exercise of religion.

answers.label: Take Care Clause
answers.explanation: Requires the president to take care that the laws be faithfully executed.

answers.label: Appointments Clause
answers.explanation: Provides the constitutional framework for appointments of federal officers.

answers.label: Treaty Clause
answers.explanation: Sets out the president’s treaty power with Senate advice and consent.

answers.label: Vesting Clause
answers.explanation: The opening provisions of Articles I, II, and III vest the powers of the branches.

answers.label: Origination Clause
answers.explanation: Revenue raising bills originate in the House.

answers.label: Presentment Clause
answers.explanation: Addresses presenting legislation to the president.

answers.label: Speech or Debate Clause
answers.explanation: Protects legislative speech and debate in Congress.

answers.label: Contract Clause
answers.explanation: Prohibits states from impairing the obligation of contracts.

answers.label: Ex Post Facto Clauses
answers.explanation: Prohibit federal and state ex post facto laws.

answers.label: Bill of Attainder Clauses
answers.explanation: Prohibit legislative bills of attainder.

answers.label: Emoluments Clauses
answers.explanation: Restrict specified benefits to federal officeholders.

answers.label: Takings Clause
answers.explanation: Requires just compensation for private property taken for public use.

answers.label: Suspension Clause
answers.explanation: Restricts suspension of the privilege of the writ of habeas corpus.

answers.label: No Religious Test Clause
answers.explanation: Forbids a religious test for federal office or public trust.

answers.label: Guarantee Clause
answers.explanation: Guarantees every state a republican form of government.

answers.label: Spending Clause
answers.explanation: Allows taxing and spending for debts, common defense, and general welfare.

answers.label: Extradition Clause
answers.explanation: Provides for interstate return of a person charged with a crime.

answers.label: Fugitive Slave Clause
answers.explanation: A historical provision superseded by the Thirteenth Amendment; it remains part of the original constitutional text.

answers.label: Three Fifths Clause
answers.explanation: The original apportionment provision was superseded by later amendments.

answers.label: Importation Clause
answers.explanation: The original text barred Congress from banning the importation of enslaved people before 1808.

answers.label: Territory Clause
answers.explanation: Grants Congress authority over federal territory and property.

answers.label: New States Clause
answers.explanation: Authorizes Congress to admit new states under Article IV.

answers.label: Commander in Chief Clause
answers.explanation: Makes the president commander in chief of the armed forces.

answers.label: Pardon Clause
answers.explanation: Gives the president the federal pardon power, except in cases of impeachment.

answers.label: Electors Clause
answers.explanation: Provides for state appointment of presidential electors.

answers.label: Elections Clause
answers.explanation: Addresses the times, places, and manner of congressional elections.

answers.label: Qualifications Clauses
answers.explanation: Set constitutional qualifications for specified federal offices.

answers.label: Congress

answers.label: House of Representatives

answers.label: Senate
answers.explanation: Article I establishes the Senate.

answers.label: Speaker of the House

answers.label: Senate impeachment trials

answers.label: Revenue bills originate in the House

answers.label: Presidential veto

answers.label: Veto override

answers.label: Bicameral passage

answers.label: Quorum

answers.label: Congressional rules

answers.label: Expulsion of members

answers.label: Congressional journals

answers.label: Speech or Debate Clause

answers.label: Appropriations

answers.label: Habeas corpus

answers.label: No bills of attainder

answers.label: No ex post facto laws

answers.label: No titles of nobility

answers.label: Foreign Emoluments Clause

answers.label: Limits on state powers

answers.label: Contract Clause

answers.label: Three Fifths Clause

answers.label: Importation Clause

prompt: Name an office, power, rule, or idea discussed in Article II of the Constitution.
hint: Think about what the original article says about this branch. Give one example.

answers.label: President
answers.explanation: Article II vests executive power in a president.

answers.label: Vice president
answers.explanation: Article II discusses the vice president and succession.

answers.label: Four year term
answers.explanation: The president serves a four year term.

answers.label: Presidential electors
answers.explanation: Article II sets out the original elector system; the Twelfth Amendment later changed parts of it.

answers.label: Presidential oath
answers.explanation: The president takes the constitutional oath.

answers.label: Natural born citizen requirement
answers.explanation: Article II sets this qualification for the presidency.

answers.label: Minimum presidential age 35
answers.explanation: A president must be at least 35 years old.

answers.label: Fourteen year residency requirement
answers.explanation: A president must have been a resident within the United States for fourteen years.

answers.label: Presidential compensation
answers.explanation: Article II protects presidential compensation from increases or decreases during the elected period and restricts other emoluments.

answers.label: Commander in chief
answers.explanation: The president commands the armed forces.

answers.label: Written opinions from department heads
answers.explanation: The president may require written opinions from principal officers of executive departments.

answers.label: Federal pardons and reprieves
answers.explanation: The president may grant reprieves and pardons for federal offenses, except in impeachment cases.

answers.label: Treaty making
answers.explanation: Treaties require the advice and consent of two thirds of senators present.

answers.label: Federal appointments
answers.explanation: Article II addresses nominations and appointments with Senate advice and consent.

answers.label: Recess appointments
answers.explanation: Article II authorizes filling certain vacancies during a Senate recess.

answers.label: State of the Union
answers.explanation: The president gives Congress information on the state of the Union from time to time.

answers.label: Recommend legislation
answers.explanation: The president recommends measures to Congress.

answers.label: Convene Congress
answers.explanation: The president may convene either or both chambers on extraordinary occasions.

answers.label: Adjourn Congress in a specified disagreement
answers.explanation: The president may adjourn Congress if the chambers disagree about the time of adjournment.

answers.label: Receive ambassadors
answers.explanation: The president receives ambassadors and other public ministers.

answers.label: Faithfully execute the laws
answers.explanation: The president must take care that the laws be faithfully executed.

answers.label: Commission federal officers
answers.explanation: The president commissions all officers of the United States.

answers.label: Removal through impeachment
answers.explanation: Article II provides removal following impeachment and conviction for specified offenses.

answers.label: Presidential succession
answers.explanation: Article II discusses succession; later amendments provide additional rules.

answers.label: Lower federal courts

answers.label: Good behavior tenure

answers.label: Federal law cases

answers.label: Treaty cases
answers.explanation: The judicial power includes cases arising under U.S. treaties.

answers.label: Ambassador cases

answers.label: Admiralty and maritime jurisdiction
answers.explanation: Article III includes admiralty and maritime cases.

answers.label: United States as a party

answers.label: Disputes between states

answers.label: Diversity jurisdiction
answers.explanation: Includes certain controversies between citizens of different states.

answers.label: State and foreign party controversies
answers.explanation: The original text includes specified controversies involving states, their citizens, and foreign parties; later amendments affect jurisdiction.

answers.label: Land grants from different states
answers.explanation: Includes claims to lands under grants of different states.

answers.label: Original jurisdiction
answers.explanation: Article III identifies categories beginning in the Supreme Court.

answers.label: Appellate jurisdiction
answers.explanation: Article III identifies appellate jurisdiction, subject to congressional exceptions and regulations.

answers.label: Exceptions and Regulations Clause
answers.explanation: Congress may make exceptions and regulations regarding the Supreme Court’s appellate jurisdiction.

answers.label: Criminal jury trials

answers.label: Place of criminal trial

answers.label: Treason

answers.label: Two witnesses for treason

answers.label: Confession in open court
answers.explanation: An open court confession is an alternative constitutional proof requirement for treason.

answers.label: Limits on punishment for treason
answers.explanation: Article III limits the effects of a treason attainder.
